title: Scan of a unary run
statement: Let $x$ be a Boolean word containing a run of $v$ true bits between a prefix and suffix. For every counter length $n$ and head position $j\le n$, arbitrary second-tape content, second-tape head position $b$, and output word $o$, starting in state $4$ with the counter head at $j$, after exactly $v$ steps the machine is again in state $4$ at the input position just after the run. The counter head is at $j+v$, the counter length is $\max(n,j+v)$, and the second tape, its head, and the output are unchanged.
replaced:
Suppose the input contains a unary run $1^v$ at the current position and the
transducer is in its index-scanning state with counter length $n$ and counter head
at $j \le n$. Then exactly $v$ steps consume the run, advancing the input by $v$,
moving the counter head to $j + v$, and extending the counter length to
$\max(n,\, j + v)$.
